title: Egypt Solo Travel Budget: Daily Costs by City
excerpt: What does a solo trip to Egypt cost per day? Sourced prices for Cairo, Luxor and Aswan: Metro, food, entrance fees, transport and shared tours from €29.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

Published 2026 estimates put a solo backpacker in Egypt at about US$30 to 50 a day and a mid-range traveller at about US$80 to 150, excluding international flights (Wego, June 2026). The big swing is guided days: Sawa's shared day tours run from €29 for about four hours to €75 for a full day, per person, as listed in November 2026. Beds, street food and the Cairo Metro cost little; entrance fees, tours and travel between cities are what move the total. This post uses only prices we can source, converted at EGP 60 to the euro (the rate on 8 November 2026), and says plainly where a price is missing.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Join it on Sawa Browse forming departures: reserving a seat is free, nothing is charged before the GoAhead

Every Egypt solo travel budget starts with the same question: what will I actually spend per day once the flight is paid? Hostel sites advertise tiny bed prices; package sites quote four-figure tours; the honest answer sits between. This post builds the answer from prices that have a source: published daily estimates, official fares and entrance fees, and the live Sawa tour listings. It is written by the team behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, who have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, so the tour costs come from real listings. Where we have no sourced price (a hostel dorm bed, a three-star room, a domestic flight fare), we do not guess one.

Egypt solo travel budget: the published daily ranges

The most useful published benchmark is Wego's 2026 budget guide, which puts a backpacker at about US$30 to 50 a day and a mid-range traveller at about US$80 to 150 a day, excluding international flights; it adds that Upper Egypt (Luxor and Aswan) is the best value for rooms and food. Treat these as third-party estimates, not quotes: Wego does not tie each figure to a single source.

Your own number depends on how many guided days you buy. A day in which you pay for a shared tour will sit at the top of a backpacker range or above it; a day of Metro rides, street food and a free afternoon sits at the bottom.

Read these as planning numbers, not quotes: Egypt revises ticket prices without much notice, and the restaurant and ride-hailing figures come from a travel site rather than an official list.

Cairo, Luxor or Aswan: which city costs more?

Cairo is the cheapest to eat in and the most expensive to move around: street food is filling and cheap, but the city is wide and traffic is real. Luxor and Aswan reverse the deal: rooms and meals are good value (Wego calls Upper Egypt the best value for both), yet the headline sites sit outside town, so guided days become your biggest daily line.

Three sample days, using only the prices above

These add up sourced prices and leave out what we cannot source, so they are floors rather than averages.

  • A guided Cairo day: Giza Uncovered €29, two short ride-hailing trips (EGP 260, about €4.30), a koshary lunch (about €0.50) and a sit-down dinner (EGP 265, about €4.40): about €38, before a bed.
  • A guided Luxor day: Luxor in Depth €75, a budget room from EGP 1,000 (€17) and a sit-down dinner (EGP 265, about €4.40): about €96, plus lunch if the departure page does not include it. Add about €12 if you want Tutankhamun's tomb.
  • An independent museum day in Cairo: the Grand Egyptian Museum (€30.50), two Metro rides (about €0.33 to €0.67), a koshary lunch (about €0.50) and a sit-down dinner (about €4.40): about €36, before a bed.

The daily costs most budgets forget

Four lines sink more Egypt budgets than room prices do: the visa, entry extras, tips and transport between cities.

  • The visa. Most visitors need a tourist visa, bought online or on arrival. The fee has changed recently and a rise has been reported for January 2027, so check the current figure on the official e-visa portal, not third-party sites that add fees.
  • Special tomb tickets. Entrance tickets are included on Sawa's Luxor and Aswan day tours as listed, but the showpiece tombs are ticketed separately: Tutankhamun's tomb is EGP 700 (about €12) on top of the Valley of the Kings ticket. Special tombs are never included on Sawa tours. The Tomb of Nefertari in the Valley of the Queens has been closed since March 2024, with no reopening date announced.
  • Pyramid interiors and camel rides. Both sit outside the Giza Uncovered price, which includes the Giza Plateau ticket. The Great Pyramid interior is EGP 1,500 (about €25); Sawa does not sell or arrange camel rides.
  • Baksheesh (tipping). Small notes for drivers, boat helpers, luggage help and site attendants. We do not give a daily figure; ask your guide what is usual.
  • Transport between cities. After your international flight, this is the biggest line in a multi-city budget. The Abela sleeper train from Cairo to Luxor costs US$110 per person in a shared Standard cabin or US$150 for a Standard cabin to yourself (Seat 61, 2026 fares), and the flight takes about an hour. We have no sourced flight fare, so check the airline.
  • Water and data. Bottled water every day in the heat, plus a local SIM or eSIM if you want maps and ride-hailing on the go. We have no sourced price for either.

How shared departures cut your biggest daily cost

Tours are the cost a solo traveller cannot shrink alone: a private guide charges per day, whether one person or ten turn up. Shared departures split that cost across a small group of four to eight travellers, with the price fixed per person and no solo surcharge on day tours. From Sawa's listings, as of November 2026:

  • Cairo: Giza Uncovered: Pyramids, Sphinx & Stories. About 4 hours, from €29 per person. The Giza Plateau entrance ticket is included, so the main extra is a pyramid interior.
  • Luxor: Luxor in Depth: East & West Bank Full Day. About 9 hours, from €75, with hotel pickup, the Nile crossing and entrance tickets included; check the departure page for lunch. Tutankhamun's tomb is a separate ticket.
  • Aswan: Aswan Highlights. About 5 hours, from €36. Motorboat to Philae, entrance tickets and lunch are included.
  • Aswan: Aswan to Abu Simbel. About 9 hours with a very early start, from €50, with hotel pickup in Aswan, an air-conditioned car on the desert road (about 280 km, 3.5 to 4 hours each way), a guide, entrance tickets and lunch. Doing Abu Simbel independently takes more organising; the road has routine checkpoints, so carry your passport.

How to do Egypt on a solo budget with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is a marketplace, not a tour operator, operated by Online Era (registration 148500). Sawa runs a fixed catalogue with fixed prices; selling agencies sell the seats; and one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date operates it, named before the deposit is due. Find a forming date or start your own on any tour page, which Sawa reviews. Reserving a seat is free, with no card, and nothing is charged until four travellers have reserved the date (the GoAhead). A 10% deposit is then paid by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241), with charges in euros, and the balance is due two days (48 hours) before departure. A date has until seven days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Cancel at least 48 hours before departure for a full refund; within 48 hours you lose the 10% deposit; force majeure brings a full refund. Cruises and packages work differently (a 25% deposit and the balance 14 days before), and solo rooms or cabins on them are confirmed in the booking. The FAQ and terms have the detail. Browse departures forming now and price your tour days before you fly.

The verdict: your Egypt solo travel budget

Egypt can be done cheaply on the ground, with a Metro ride under €0.35 and a budget room in Luxor from about €17, and the guiding is the line to plan around. Shared day tours keep that line at group prices with no solo surcharge: from €29 for a half day to €75 for a full day. faq.q: How much money do I need per day in Egypt?
faq.a: Published 2026 estimates run from about US$30 to 50 a day for a backpacker to about US$80 to 150 for mid-range travel, excluding international flights (Wego, June 2026). A day with a Sawa shared tour adds €29 to €75 per person, depending on the tour. Add the visa (check the fee on the official e-visa portal) and your flights on top.

faq.q: Is Egypt a cheap destination for solo travellers?
faq.a: Compared with most of Europe, mostly yes: a Metro ride costs EGP 10 to 20 (about €0.17 to €0.33), a budget koshary plate about EGP 30 (about €0.50) and a budget room in Luxor from about EGP 1,000 (about €17). The catch for solo travellers is tours: private guides often price per booking, not per person, which can multiply your sightseeing costs. Shared departures fix that by splitting one guide and vehicle across a small group.

faq.q: Should I carry cash or card in Egypt?
faq.a: Carry both. Cards are usually accepted at hotels and larger restaurants, but street food, microbuses, ferries and tips run on Egyptian pounds in cash. Withdraw from bank ATMs in cities rather than changing money on the street, and keep small notes for baksheesh.

faq.q: Do solo travellers pay more for tours in Egypt?
faq.a: On private tours, often yes, because operators price per vehicle or per guide. On Sawa shared day tours, no: the price is fixed per traveller with no solo surcharge, and departures are capped at eight travellers. On cruises and packages, solo rooms and cabins are confirmed in the booking. You reserve a seat free and pay a 10% deposit only once the date confirms at four travellers.

faq.q: What happens if my shared departure never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A date confirms only when four travellers have reserved it, and has until seven days before the tour to get there. If it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing and Sawa suggests another date. Once a date confirms, it is not cancelled for low numbers.

faq.q: How much should I budget for tipping in Egypt?
faq.a: Budget small notes rather than big amounts: baksheesh is part of daily life, covering drivers, boat helpers, bathroom attendants and luggage help. Tipping your Egyptologist guide at the end of a tour is customary but discretionary. We have no sourced daily figure, so ask your guide or operator what is usual.
